close_reason:
Superseded by bd:JMAP-qz9v.35 close + correction of the bead's PROPAGATION premise.

The bead's analysis is technically accurate ('value: serde_json::Value parameter exposes the MemoryBackend's internal storage representation') but its recommended reshape (typed 'seed<O: JmapObject + Serialize>') conflicts with three workspace facts visible at HEAD:

1. seed_object exists across the 3 sibling MemoryBackend impls that have a seeding API (calendars-server, contacts-server, tasks-server) — NOT just contacts-server as the bead's PROPAGATION section claims. The 'Value' shape is therefore workspace-canonical, not a contacts-server divergence. (Canonical mail-server has no seed_object at all, but the 3 sibling crates that do all use the Value shape.)

2. The internal storage choice 'HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>' is universal across all 8 sibling extension-server MemoryBackend impls — it's the canonical reference-impl pattern, not a contacts-specific implementation detail. The 'Value' parameter is the same shape as the wire-format JSON serde produces from any typed object, so a caller's 'typed_obj -> serde_json::to_value(&typed_obj)' is one trivial line at the call site.

3. The validation gap the bead actually worries about ('a JMAP-objectish-but-not-quite Value seeded in tests') was closed by bd:JMAP-qz9v.35 (just landed): seed_object now panics at the seed boundary on type-name typos, non-object values, and id mismatches with actionable error messages. The 'typed at compile time' goal is met by the validation, in a way that preserves the deliberate use case the bead's reshape would foreclose:

   DELIBERATE USE CASE the reshape would break: test fixtures that seed partial / malformed / vendor-extras-containing Values to exercise edge cases in handlers (missing server-set field; unknown field; pre-validation-pattern stale fixture). A typed 'seed<O: Serialize>' parameter forces the caller to construct a fully-typed object first, defeating the test-fixture flexibility that's the entire point of having seed_object separate from the production /set path.

Conclusion: the bead's concern (silent fixture corruption surfaces far from the seed call site as opaque MemoryError) is the right concern, but the right fix is the validation pattern (.35), not the typed-parameter reshape. Closing as superseded; if a future workspace decision wants typed-from-day-one regardless of the test-fixture flexibility cost, the right framing is a new workspace-architectural epic that touches the canonical mail-server FIRST and propagates to all 3 sibling crates, not a contacts-local fix.
description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:251-266

SIGNATURE:
    pub fn seed_object(
        &self,
        account_id: &str,
        type_name: &'static str,
        id: &str,
        value: serde_json::Value,    // ← leaks internal storage shape
    )

PROBLEM:
The `value: serde_json::Value` parameter exposes the MemoryBackend's
internal storage representation (objects-as-Value) as part of its
public API. The `Inner.objects` field at memory.rs:121 is typed as
`HashMap<(&'static str, String), HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>>` —
this storage choice was made for the in-memory reference impl, but
shipping `seed_object(value: serde_json::Value)` forecloses ever
switching to typed storage (e.g., HashMap<Id, AddressBook>) without
a breaking API change to seed_object.

The cookie-cutter argument that "this is the reference impl, so its
internals are public anyway" is wrong. The reference impl is gated
behind `feature = "memory"`, documented as "API stability is opt-in
via this feature and may break across minor versions while the crate
is pre-1.0" (lib.rs:23-27, memory.rs:23-24). But that escape hatch
applies to the WHOLE module — it does not specifically signal that
seed_object's serde_json::Value parameter is a known leak. A reader
sees an opt-in feature and assumes typical Rust API stability rules
apply per item within that feature.

The leak compounds with JMAP-qz9v.24 (stringly-typed type_name):
together, the seed_object signature says "give me any blob of JSON
under any type name string and trust the runtime to align them"
rather than "seed a typed fixture". A future where seed_object takes
`O: JmapObject + Serialize` and validates at compile time is closed.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That the internal storage format will not change (it might; the
  serde_json::Value parameter is the only thing pinning it down).
- That a JMAP-objectish-but-not-quite Value seeded in their tests
  will round-trip through get_objects::<O>.

EVIDENCE OF FRAGILITY:
crate-jmap-contacts-server/tests/contacts_tests.rs uses seed_object
with hand-built json!({...}) fixtures (e.g. address_book_fixture at
line 23-39). These fixtures encode the wire-format shape (camelCase,
@type discriminators, etc.) and DO match what the storage layer
expects, but the match is unverified at seed time. JMAP-qz9v.30
covers the matching defensive-code finding.

RECOMMENDED:
Change the signature to typed seeding:

    pub fn seed<O>(&self, account_id: &Id, id: &Id, obj: &O)
    where
        O: JmapObject + Serialize,
    {
        let value = serde_json::to_value(obj)
            .expect("derive(Serialize) on JmapObject is infallible");
        // ... internal handling
    }

Callers write:
    backend.seed::<AddressBook>(&Id::from("acc1"), &Id::from("ab1"),
                                &AddressBook { ... });

— typed, explicit, no internal-shape leak. The internal
serde-to-Value conversion stays an implementation detail.

PROPAGATION: this helper exists only in contacts-server, not in the
canonical jmap-mail-server. Either drop it or propagate the typed
shape (above) to the canonical and the 5 other extension siblings
in the same pass. The current state is a cookie-cutter regression.
title: MemoryBackend::seed_object exposes serde_json::Value as storage shape — locks reference impl to JSON-stored representation
